opening.text: An electrician can have all the right tools and still have no light. The wires must connect to the power source. The priesthood is like that. It is not a title or a role. It is God's power and authority, given to people so they can bless others.

mainMessage.text: The priesthood is the power and authority of God. It was restored, it has keys, and it is used to bless everyone.

blocks.text: **Called of God** No one takes this authority on his own. God calls, and the person is ordained by those who hold authority.
And no man taketh this honour unto himself, but he that is called of God, as was Aaron.

Ye have not chosen me, but I have chosen you, and ordained you, that ye should go and bring forth fruit, and that your fruit should remain: that whatsoever ye shall ask of the Father in my name, he may give it you.
President Dallin H. Oaks, First Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “The Powers of the Priesthood” from the April 2018 general conference.
When one becomes a holder of the priesthood, he becomes an agent of the Lord.
An agent acts for someone else. That is the point.
**Sent back from heaven** The authority was lost. Then it was restored by heavenly messengers, starting with John the Baptist.

Upon you my fellow servants, in the name of Messiah I confer the Priesthood of Aaron, which holds the keys of the ministering of angels, and of the gospel of repentance, and of baptism by immersion for the remission of sins; and this shall never be taken again from the earth, until the sons of Levi do offer again an offering unto the Lord in righteousness.

The messenger who visited us on this occasion and conferred this Priesthood upon us, said that his name was John, the same that is called John the Baptist in the New Testament, and that he acted under the direction of Peter, James and John, who held the keys of the Priesthood of Melchizedek, which Priesthood, he said, would in due time be conferred on us, and that I should be called the first Elder of the Church, and he (Oliver Cowdery) the second. It was on the fifteenth day of May, 1829, that we were ordained under the hand of this messenger, and baptized.
President Russell M. Nelson, President of the Church, said this in his talk “Rejoice in the Gift of Priesthood Keys” from the April 2024 general conference.
Let us rejoice that priesthood keys are once again on the earth!
This was not invented. It was given.
**The keys** Keys decide who may use the authority, and how. The higher priesthood holds the keys of the knowledge of God.
And this greater priesthood administereth the gospel and holdeth the key of the mysteries of the kingdom, even the key of the knowledge of God.
President Russell M. Nelson, President of the Church, said this in his talk “Rejoice in the Gift of Priesthood Keys” from the April 2024 general conference.
Priesthood keys constitute the authority and power of presidency.
There is order in God's house. Keys keep it that way.
**Power in the ordinances** Baptism, the sacrament, the temple and blessings all need priesthood authority. Through these, God's power reaches us.

Therefore, in the ordinances thereof, the power of godliness is manifest. And without the ordinances thereof, and the authority of the priesthood, the power of godliness is not manifest unto men in the flesh; For without this no man can see the face of God, even the Father, and live.
President Russell M. Nelson, President of the Church, said this in his talk “Rejoice in the Gift of Priesthood Keys” from the April 2024 general conference.
Priesthood keys distinguish The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints from any other organization on earth.
The ordinances are not tradition. They are doors.
**Used with righteousness** Priesthood power is not for pride or control. The Lord set a clear rule.
That the rights of the priesthood are inseparably connected with the powers of heaven, and that the powers of heaven cannot be controlled nor handled only upon the principles of righteousness.

No power or influence can or ought to be maintained by virtue of the priesthood, only by persuasion, by long-suffering, by gentleness and meekness, and by love unfeigned; By kindness, and pure knowledge, which shall greatly enlarge the soul without hypocrisy, and without guile—
President Dallin H. Oaks, First Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “The Powers of the Priesthood” from the April 2018 general conference.
It is a divine power held in trust to use for the benefit of God’s work for His children.
Held in trust means we do not own it. We serve with it.
**A blessing for all** The priesthood is meant to bless every nation, every family and every person.

And I will make of thee a great nation, and I will bless thee above measure, and make thy name great among all nations, and thou shalt be a blessing unto thy seed after thee, that in their hands they shall bear this ministry and Priesthood unto all nations;
President Dallin H. Oaks, First Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “The Melchizedek Priesthood and the Keys” from the April 2020 general conference.
The power of the priesthood exists both in the Church and in the family organization.
It belongs in the home as much as in the chapel.

blocks.text: God asked Moses to bring Aaron and his sons to serve as priests.

And take thou unto thee Aaron thy brother, and his sons with him, from among the children of Israel, that he may minister unto me in the priest’s office, even Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar, Aaron’s sons.
Aaron did not choose this role. God did. This has always been God's pattern. He calls, and He gives the authority. And the purpose is to minister, which means to serve.

blocks.text: The early Church needed help. They chose seven good men. The apostles prayed and laid their hands on them.

story.title: The centurion's faith

blocks.text: A Roman officer asked Jesus to heal his servant. He understood authority better than anyone.

The centurion answered and said, Lord, I am not worthy that thou shouldest come under my roof: but speak the word only, and my servant shall be healed. For I am a man under authority, having soldiers under me: and I say to this man, Go, and he goeth; and to another, Come, and he cometh; and to my servant, Do this, and he doeth it. When Jesus heard it, he marvelled, and said to them that followed, Verily I say unto you, I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel.
The centurion knew that real authority comes from above, and that it works. He trusted Jesus Christ's authority fully. We can too.

story.title: A pattern for those who serve

blocks.text: The Lord gave a simple pattern for how to hold His power.

Let thy bowels also be full of charity towards all men, and to the household of faith, and let virtue garnish thy thoughts unceasingly; then shall thy confidence wax strong in the presence of God; and the doctrine of the priesthood shall distil upon thy soul as the dews from heaven.
Charity and virtue come first. Then confidence comes. Then the doctrine of the priesthood comes quietly, like dew. This is how keepers are made.

application.text: First, choose one way to show more charity this week. Second, watch your thoughts and keep them clean. Third, pray for confidence in the presence of God.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know the priesthood is God's light and that He trusts us to tend it. I know it was restored. I know it blesses homes and nations. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

invitations: I invite you to choose one way to show more charity this week.
I invite you to watch your thoughts and keep them clean.
I invite you to pray for confidence in the presence of God.
blessings: Your heart will be filled with charity.
The Holy Ghost will be your constant companion.

closingVerse.text: But charity is the pure love of Christ, and it endureth forever; and whoso is found possessed of it at the last day, it shall be well with him.
